name: Kayla Itsines
who: Co-founder of Sweat, the global women's fitness app built on her BBG program; sells subscription-based coached training plans across strength, cardio, and postpartum tracks.
why: Built and scaled the largest women's fitness app in the world, reaching over 30 million subscribers; sold Sweat for a nine-figure sum and later reacquired the business.
takeaway: Build one signature program, then scale it into a subscription app — the program is the business.

name: Krissy Cela
who: Co-founder and lead trainer of EvolveYou (formerly Tone and Sculpt), a strength-training coaching app with structured, personalized programs.
why: Turned a personal-training background into one of the UK's top women's fitness apps, staying hands-on as lead trainer.
takeaway: Stay hands-on as lead trainer even after scaling — presence keeps the product credible.

name: Caroline Girvan
who: Personal trainer and nutritionist behind the free EPIC YouTube programs and the paid CGX app, which sells structured strength programming and nutrition guidance.
why: One of the most-watched home-workout program creators for women, with a dedicated coaching app extending her free YouTube series into paid, ongoing programming.
takeaway: Give the workout away free on YouTube, then sell the ongoing structure and progression as the app.

name: Natacha Oceane
who: Biophysicist and trainer who sells structured strength/endurance programs, including HYBRID, through the Aflete coaching app.
why: Rare combination of academic rigor (UCL biophysics, Team GB-linked programming) and a genuine coaching product; content is trusted for scientific accuracy.
takeaway: Let your academic background back every claim — accuracy is the trust that sells the program.

name: Bret Contreras
who: PhD biomechanist known as 'The Glute Guy' who sells Booty by Bret, an online strength program for women built from his own client programming.
why: Inventor of the barbell hip thrust and one of the most credentialed glute-training researchers; his program uses the same workouts he runs with real clients.
takeaway: Sell the exact program you run with real clients — don't water down what actually works.

name: Senada Greca
who: Founder of WeRise, an all-in-one women's fitness and wellness app covering strength, Pilates, yoga, nutrition, and cycle-syncing.
why: Built one of the most-downloaded women's fitness apps in 2026 off a large, highly engaged personal following.
takeaway: Cover the whole picture in one app — strength, nutrition, and cycle-syncing together, not separate products.

name: Kelsey Wells
who: Sweat global trainer and creator of PWR, a weight-training program for women delivered through the Sweat app.
why: PWR ranked among Sweat's top three most-downloaded training guides in 2026; built a large following around strength training for women specifically.
takeaway: Own a niche inside a bigger platform — strength training for women became its own top-ranked lane.

name: Alexia Clark
who: 'Queen of Workouts' and founder of the Alexia Clark app, which sells weekly workouts, a nutrition plan, and direct personal support from Alexia.
why: Built a large, loyal 'QueenTeam' community and a subscription coaching app with genuine 1:1 access, not just templated content.
takeaway: Give the community a name and direct personal access — a loyal 'team' identity keeps subscribers renewing.

name: Meg Squats (Meg Gallagher)
who: Strength and conditioning coach, founder of Stronger by the Day, a membership lifting program and coaching collective for women.
why: Has personally coached tens of thousands of strength athletes from their first squat to national-level meets; long-running, community-driven coaching brand rather than a passive content feed.
takeaway: Build a community members grow inside — from first squat to competition, not a passive feed.

name: Linn Lowes
who: Swedish fitness entrepreneur and cancer survivor who founded the Athli App, offering customizable gym and home workout programs plus nutrition plans.
why: Converted a large personal following into a self-built coaching platform with over 20 workout programs and thousands of recipes.
takeaway: Convert a personal story and following into a self-built platform, not someone else's white-label app.

name: Anna Engelschall (growingannanas)
who: Certified trainer and former CrossFit coach who founded Grow With Anna, an app with personalized strength, HIIT, and full-body training plans; CEO of The Grow Lifestyle GmbH.
why: One of the largest women's home-workout YouTube channels, converted into a dedicated coaching-app business.
takeaway: Convert your YouTube audience into a paid app — the channel proves demand before you build.

name: Danyele Wilson
who: Tone & Sculpt (EvolveYou) HIIT trainer and founder of the SPARC app, combining workouts with mindset training.
why: Corporate-marketing-turned-fitness-coach whose body-positive coaching and personal story built a devoted, engaged following.
takeaway: Combine workouts with mindset training and tell your own career-change story to build a devoted following.

name: Brianna Battles
who: Founder of the Pregnancy & Postpartum Athleticism Coalition (PPAC), running coaching and certification programs for pre/postnatal athletes and the coaches who train them.
why: Leading voice in pre/postnatal return-to-training coaching, widely cited among strength and CrossFit coaches for a rigorous, athlete-specific framework.
reach: IG ~150K (approx, not independently verified this session)
takeaway: Build a rigorous framework for an underserved population, then certify other coaches to deliver it.

name: Emily Skye
who: Founder of the Emily Skye FIT app, selling structured strength and postpartum-inclusive training programs for women.
why: One of the earliest fitness-app founders in this space, with a large, long-standing global following built well before the current wave of coaching apps.
reach: IG ~2.8M (approx, not independently verified this session)
takeaway: Move early into app-based coaching — being first in a niche builds a following that lasts.

name: Massy Arias
who: Personal trainer and mental-health advocate running her own online coaching programs for women.
why: Known for pairing strength coaching with mental-health advocacy, building a highly engaged, mission-driven community rather than a purely aesthetic following.
reach: IG ~1.8M (approx, not independently verified this session)
takeaway: Pair strength coaching with mental-health advocacy — a mission-driven community engages deeper than aesthetics.

name: Cassey Ho (Blogilates)
who: Founder of Blogilates and its companion training app, plus POPFLEX activewear; sells structured Pilates-based workout programs and calendars.
why: Built one of the largest women's fitness media-and-coaching businesses from POP Pilates, with a decade-plus, highly engaged following.
reach: YT 5.9M · IG 2M+ (approx, not independently verified this session)
takeaway: Stay consistent for a decade — a single format repeated builds a loyal, decade-long following.

name: Stefi Cohen
who: Doctor of physical therapy, world-record powerlifter, and co-founder of Hybrid Performance Method (HPM), a large team-based online coaching business.
why: Elite competitive record (multiple all-time world records) paired with a scaled coaching team; a rare combination of athletic and clinical credibility.
reach: IG ~1.5M (approx, not independently verified this session)
takeaway: Combine clinical training with athletic proof — credentials and competition results reinforce each other.

name: Amanda Bucci
who: Certified nutrition and fitness coach running Bucci Fit, an online 1:1 and group coaching business for women.
why: Solo coach with a thriving, personality-driven brand blending nutrition coaching, business content, and fitness.
reach: IG ~700K (approx, not independently verified this session)
takeaway: Blend business content with fitness coaching — a personality-driven brand can serve more than one interest.
